newsitem.title: USA: CME live and feeder cattle end up, set new highs.
newsitem.headline: CME live and feeder cattle end up, set new highs.

text.p: Profit taking and rolling of long positions continued to weigh on nearby CME live cattle futures, but demand from strong cash held prices kept values firm at the close after futures set fresh contract highs.

October live cattle set a new high of 73.300 cents per lb, the fourth consecutive contract high, before closing up 0.100 at 73.275 cents. December also set a new high of 68.900 cents and closed 0.275 higher at 68.875 cents. Other months finished 0.175 cent higher to unchanged.
October feeders set a new high of 64.950 cents and ended up 0.575 at 64.850 cents. Other months were up 0.375 to 0.200.
The strong tone to cash markets underpinned live cattle futures despite the spread action, partly attributed to fund rolling commonly know as the "Goldman roll".
"We had record movement of cattle again this week in the cash trade and that just underpins this market," said Don Roose, President of U.S. Commodities Inc.

USDA reported a record 196,000 head movement in the Texas/Oklahoma panhandle trade. Even though live trade is seen light next week after the big movement, cash prices will hold strong as feedlots are very current. Fed numbers are down due to low cattle placements into feedyards earlier this year.
"The packer realizes that we are coming into numbers here that are documentedly tight, so they are keeping cattle numbers around them" to meet kill needs, Roose said.

Early projections on next Friday's USDA Cattle-on-Feed report put the number of cattle on feed as of Sept 1 at 88.2 to 92 percent of a year ago, while placements were tabbed at 110.2 to 115.8 percent and marketings at 92 to 97.2 percent.

Merrill Lynch notably spread long December/short October while RBH spread long February/short October early. Refco spread long December/short October late. R.J. O'Brien bought October while Cargill Investor Services and Shatkin Lit Division of First Options bought December, pit sources said.
In live cattle options, volatility was steady to weak. There was continued commercial hedge interest in back months, pit sources added.
Feeders showed strength most of the day on losses in corn futures and the strong tone to fed cattle markets.
"There is aggressive interest in feeder cattle right here, particularly as we get closer to the corn crop (harvest)," Roose said.
Buying by R.J. O'Brien and locals touched off commission house buy stops in October during the day, traders said.
